item.title: [NEW LAW] [Publication] Data centres forced to generate more power than they use under new laws
item.description: Business and tech leaders have welcomed Prime Minister Anthony Albanese’s ambition to establish Australia as a global leader in artificial intelligence, but warn that flawed policy execution could jeopardise the foreign investment required to achieve it. In a speech at the University of Sydney on Wednesday, the prime minister reversed Labor’s hands-off approach to Artificial Intelligence (AI) regulation by announcing a new Office of AI within his own department, and new legislated Australian AI standards that would include the need for large-scale data centres to generate as much power as they use.

item.title: [ENFORCEMENT] [Publication] CCPA fines SpiceJet ₹1 lakh for using dark patterns to obtain consumer consent for loyalty programme
item.description: The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed a penalty of ₹1 lakh on SpiceJet for using pre-ticked checkboxes to enrol consumers in its loyalty programme and obtain their consent for promotional communications. Chief Commissioner Nidhi Khare and Commissioner Anupam Mishra held that SpiceJet’s booking interface impaired consumer autonomy and amounted to an unfair trade practice, an unfair contract and a misleading advertisement under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

item.title: [ANALYSIS] [Law Firm] Two eras, one rulebook what agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) does to your General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) compliance - Bird & Bird
item.description: One task, 4 sub-calls, 4 different General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) roles, and a Data Protection Authority (DPA) that called all 4 processors. You can’t outsource controllership. But if you don’t vet the chain, the chain decides your role for you. What to do: map every data flow per agent (which third parties, what data, which direction); classify each actor at each step; refresh vendor DPAs to cover dynamically selected sub-processors, agent memory, mid-process cross-border transfers and audit rights over agent behaviour; and update your ROPA and privacy notices, because new recipients, retention periods and automated decisions each may trigger fresh transparency obligations.
